about.title: Lot sizes vary, and the ground **is heavy.**
body: Mundy Township sits west of Grand Blanc, between Flint and Fenton, and most of its land is homes and farms. Homes here run newer than in the older towns around Flint, and about a quarter of them were built in 2000 or later.

Lot sizes swing widely. Under the township zoning, a home without sewer in the residential agricultural districts needs at least an acre, while sewered lots can be as small as 14,000 or 20,000 square feet, and cluster subdivisions smaller still. One street can mean a quick weekly cut and the next a long afternoon on a zero turn.
Much of the ground is heavy soils that drain slowly, and the flood plains along Swartz Creek and the county drains are wetter still. Lawns there stay soft after a rain and into spring.

points.title: County roads, county plows
points.body: The Genesee County Road Commission looks after the roads here and plows by traffic: expressways, then main roads, then local roads, with subdivision streets last. It does not give times for any one street.

points.title: Yard waste goes out Tuesdays
points.body: Republic Services collects curbside on Tuesdays. From April through November, yard waste goes in Kraft paper bags or a marked 30 gallon can, no plastic, and large bushes, stumps and trunks are not taken.

points.title: Leaves may not be burned
points.body: The township fire department allows burning only logs, limbs, stumps and brush, with a permit. Leaf rakings and ground cover are on its list of things that may not be burned.

points.title: Big jobs leave in our trailer
points.body: The township's monthly landfill permit does not take yard waste, trees, limbs or bushes either. Whatever we cut, rake or dig out, we haul away ourselves.

logistics.title: How we work in Mundy Township.
body: Call or text Rob at [(810) 990-3040](tel:+18109903040) or send the [estimate form](/get-an-estimate/). He comes out, walks the property with you, suggests what it needs and gives you a price at no charge.

The township sits just west of Grand Blanc Township, about 15 minutes from our shop on Embury Road. Mowing runs weekly on a set day, cleanups follow the weather and the ground, and winter service gets set up with Rob before the first snow.

Start with [lawn mowing](/lawn-mowing-mundy-township-mi/), [spring cleanup](/spring-cleanup-mundy-township-mi/), [leaf removal](/leaf-removal-mundy-township-mi/), [landscaping](/landscaping-mundy-township-mi/) or [snow removal](/snow-removal-mundy-township-mi/), or see every [service](/services/) we offer.

faq.q: Do you do lawn care and snow removal in Mundy Township?
faq.a: Yes. Grand Scapes mows, does spring and fall cleanups, rebuilds beds and plows driveways in Mundy Township, MI, and the estimate is free.

faq.q: My address says Swartz Creek or Flint. Am I in Mundy Township?
faq.a: Possibly. Homes in the township carry Flint, Swartz Creek, Fenton, Grand Blanc or Holly mailing addresses, and the township hall itself uses a Swartz Creek address. Your tax bill or the township office will confirm it. We work in all of those areas either way.

faq.q: Who plows the roads in Mundy Township?
faq.a: The Genesee County Road Commission. It plows expressways first, then main roads, then local roads, and subdivision streets last, and it says it cannot give a time for any one street. Your driveway is up to you, which is where our [snow removal](/snow-removal-mundy-township-mi/) comes in.

faq.q: Can I burn leaves in Mundy Township?
faq.a: No. The township fire department's burn permit rules allow only logs, limbs, stumps and brush, and they list leaf rakings and ground cover among the things that may not be burned. A [fall cleanup](/leaf-removal-mundy-township-mi/) hauls the leaves off instead.

faq.q: Why does my yard stay wet after a rain?
faq.a: Because most of the township sits on heavy soil that drains slowly, and land near the creek and the drains is wetter still. If a low spot never dries out, ask Rob about [grading](/grading-and-new-lawns/).
